description:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-12 in crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop, per explicit maintainer decision.

DECISION. OPCPFluidArray is a PIPE: its ends are junctions with a flow network, not patches on a standalone 3-D domain. It therefore uses the TUAS boundary-condition convention (upwind advection terminals) rather than generic OpenFOAM zeroGradient/fixedValue patch semantics.

THE DEFECT THIS REPLACES. The explicit energy convection fvc::div evaluated every boundary face from its BC TYPE alone. Two failure modes, both reachable:
- zero-gradient on an INFLOW face advects the domain's own enthalpy inwards (h_face = h_owner): self-referential, and with zero-gradient at both ends there is no boundary through which energy can enter or leave, so mdot*(h_out - h_in) = Q cannot even be posed. This is the state the array was left in before the he BC re-stamp (op-2qsf), which restored the VALUE while leaving the FORMULATION direction-agnostic.
- fixed-value on an OUTFLOW face forces the enthalpy the domain is exporting, which the domain does not get to choose. This is what a flow reversal produces from a correctly-set-up forward case.

PORTED LOGIC. From tuas_boussinesq_solver/src/lib/single_control_vol/boundary_condition_interactions/advection_to_bcs.rs -- its advection_heat_rate takes h_a when mdot_{a->b} >= 0 and h_b otherwise, and its calculate_*_advection_set_temperature / _non_set_temperature pair supplies the boundary-side enthalpy either from a prescribed BC state or from a zero-gradient extrapolation. In FV terms, with phi positive OUT of the domain:
    phi_b >= 0 (outflow, interior upstream) -> psi_f = psi_owner
    phi_b <  0 (inflow,  boundary upstream) -> psi_f = BC-evaluated face value
Implemented in openfoam_source::fv_operators::fvc::div_limited. Equivalent to OpenFOAM's inletOutlet, and it matches the vendored IMPLICIT fvm::div, which already switched on the flux sign -- only the explicit operator did not.

NO FORMULATION MISMATCH. The concern that a matrix/patch FV formulation could not express a lumped control-volume convention did not materialise: the selection is per face per call inside the explicit convection operator, needs no matrix-structure change, and a zero-gradient patch degenerates exactly to TUAS's non-set-temperature terminal.

API (additive; no signature changes, no version bump):
  set_outlet_enthalpy / get_outlet_advected_enthalpy / get_inlet_advected_enthalpy
  set_inlet_enthalpy KEEPS its signature but changes MEANING: it is now the upstream state used only while fluid enters through that end, ignored on outflow (inletOutlet), where before it was an unconditional Dirichlet value. Documented on the method.

VERIFICATION. flow_reversal_keeps_enthalpy_bounded_by_both_end_states: 8 cells, seed 400 K, left-end state 300 K, right-end state 500 K, +/-0.5 m/s switching every 2500 steps, 4 phases (two full reversals). Worst overshoot and worst undershoot both +0.00 kJ/kg across all 10000 steps. Forward flow settles the inlet cell to 301.7 K (the 300 K left state); after reversal the far cell settles to 499.9 K (the 500 K right state) -- each end supplies its own prescribed state exactly when it is upstream.

COORDINATION. tampines-steam-tables' TampinesSteamArray needs the same change; another agent owns that crate.
title: OPCPFluidArray: pipe ends are now direction-switched advection terminals (TUAS convention), not OpenFOAM patches (DONE)

description: Detect boundary loops (edges incident to exactly one face) and cap each with a centroid-fan triangulation, making an open surface watertight. Blender analogue: bmo_holes_fill / Fill Holes. Winding of each cap triangle is chosen opposite to the boundary directed edge so it stays consistent with the existing surface (adjacent faces traverse the shared edge in opposite directions). Directly serves the MC CSG bridge, which needs closed geometry. New MeshOp::FillHoles variant + dispatch. Pairs with weld (op-hzs.22): weld stitches near-coincident seams, fill-holes closes true gaps. V&V: cube with one face removed -> chi back to 2, watertight (every edge borders 2 faces); an already-closed mesh is a no-op.
title: outram-blender: fill holes (cap open boundary loops -> watertight)
